006
007import java.util.function.BiFunction;
008import org.ejml.dense.row.decomposition.qr.QRDecompositionHouseholder_DDRM;
009import org.ejml.simple.SimpleMatrix;
010import org.wpilib.math.linalg.Matrix;
011import org.wpilib.math.numbers.N1;
012import org.wpilib.math.system.Discretization;
013import org.wpilib.math.system.NumericalIntegration;
014import org.wpilib.math.system.NumericalJacobian;
015import org.wpilib.math.util.MathSharedStore;

021/**
022 * A Kalman filter combines predictions from a model and measurements to give an estimate of the
023 * true system state. This is useful because many states cannot be measured directly as a result of
024 * sensor noise, or because the state is "hidden".
025 *
026 * <p>This class's constructors require a SigmaPoints generator. For convenience, {@link S3UKF} and
027 * {@link MerweUKF} subclasses are provided to create a suitable generator for you. S3UKF is
028 * generally preferred over MerweUKF because of its greater performance while maintaining nearly
029 * identical accuracy.
030 *
031 * <p>Kalman filters use a K gain matrix to determine whether to trust the model or measurements
032 * more. Kalman filter theory uses statistics to compute an optimal K gain which minimizes the sum
033 * of squares error in the state estimate. This K gain is used to correct the state estimate by some
034 * amount of the difference between the actual measurements and the measurements predicted by the
035 * model.
036 *
037 * <p>An unscented Kalman filter uses nonlinear state and measurement models. It propagates the
038 * error covariance using sigma points chosen to approximate the true probability distribution.
039 *
040 * <p>For more on the underlying math, read <a
041 * href="https://file.tavsys.net/control/controls-engineering-in-frc.pdf">https://file.tavsys.net/control/controls-engineering-in-frc.pdf</a>
042 * chapter 9 "Stochastic control theory".
043 *
044 * <p>This class implements a square-root-form unscented Kalman filter (SR-UKF). The main reason for
045 * this is to guarantee that the covariance matrix remains positive definite. For more information
046 * about the SR-UKF, see https://www.researchgate.net/publication/3908304.
047 *
048 * @param <States> Number of states.
049 * @param <Inputs> Number of inputs.
050 * @param <Outputs> Number of outputs.
051 */
052public class UnscentedKalmanFilter<States extends Num, Inputs extends Num, Outputs extends Num>
053    implements KalmanTypeFilter<States, Inputs, Outputs> {
054  private final Nat<States> m_states;
055  private final Nat<Outputs> m_outputs;
056
057  private final BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> m_f;
058  private final BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>> m_h;
059
060  private BiFunction<Matrix<States, ?>, Matrix<?, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> m_meanFuncX;
061  private BiFunction<Matrix<Outputs, ?>, Matrix<?, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>> m_meanFuncY;
062  private BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> m_residualFuncX;
063  private BiFunction<Matrix<Outputs, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>> m_residualFuncY;
064  private BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> m_addFuncX;
065
066  private Matrix<States, N1> m_xHat;
067  private Matrix<States, States> m_S;
068  private final Matrix<States, States> m_contQ;
069  private final Matrix<Outputs, Outputs> m_contR;
070  private Matrix<States, ?> m_sigmasF;
071  private double m_dt;
072
073  private final SigmaPoints<States> m_pts;
074
075  /**
076   * Constructs an Unscented Kalman Filter.
077   *
078   * <p>See <a
079   * href="https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-controls/state-space/state-space-observers.html#process-and-measurement-noise-covariance-matrices">https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-controls/state-space/state-space-observers.html#process-and-measurement-noise-covariance-matrices</a>
080   * for how to select the standard deviations.
081   *
082   * @param pts A sigma points and weights generator.
083   * @param states A Nat representing the number of states.
084   * @param outputs A Nat representing the number of outputs.
085   * @param f A vector-valued function of x and u that returns the derivative of the state vector.
086   * @param h A vector-valued function of x and u that returns the measurement vector.
087   * @param stateStdDevs Standard deviations of model states.
088   * @param measurementStdDevs Standard deviations of measurements.
089   * @param nominalDt Nominal discretization timestep in seconds.
090   */
091  public UnscentedKalmanFilter(
092      SigmaPoints<States> pts,
093      Nat<States> states,
094      Nat<Outputs> outputs,
095      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> f,
096      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>> h,
097      Matrix<States, N1> stateStdDevs,
098      Matrix<Outputs, N1> measurementStdDevs,
099      double nominalDt) {
100    this(
101        pts,
102        states,
103        outputs,
104        f,
105        h,
106        stateStdDevs,
107        measurementStdDevs,
108        (sigmas, Wm) -> sigmas.times(Matrix.changeBoundsUnchecked(Wm)),
109        (sigmas, Wm) -> sigmas.times(Matrix.changeBoundsUnchecked(Wm)),
110        Matrix::minus,
111        Matrix::minus,
112        Matrix::plus,
113        nominalDt);
114  }
115
116  /**
117   * Constructs an Unscented Kalman filter with custom mean, residual, and addition functions. Using
118   * custom functions for arithmetic can be useful if you have angles in the state or measurements,
119   * because they allow you to correctly account for the modular nature of angle arithmetic.
120   *
121   * <p>See <a
122   * href="https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-controls/state-space/state-space-observers.html#process-and-measurement-noise-covariance-matrices">https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-controls/state-space/state-space-observers.html#process-and-measurement-noise-covariance-matrices</a>
123   * for how to select the standard deviations.
124   *
125   * @param pts A sigma points and weights generator.
126   * @param states A Nat representing the number of states.
127   * @param outputs A Nat representing the number of outputs.
128   * @param f A vector-valued function of x and u that returns the derivative of the state vector.
129   * @param h A vector-valued function of x and u that returns the measurement vector.
130   * @param stateStdDevs Standard deviations of model states.
131   * @param measurementStdDevs Standard deviations of measurements.
132   * @param meanFuncX A function that computes the mean of NumSigmas state vectors using a given set
133   *     of weights.
134   * @param meanFuncY A function that computes the mean of NumSigmas measurement vectors using a
135   *     given set of weights.
136   * @param residualFuncX A function that computes the residual of two state vectors (i.e. it
137   *     subtracts them.)
138   * @param residualFuncY A function that computes the residual of two measurement vectors (i.e. it
139   *     subtracts them.)
140   * @param addFuncX A function that adds two state vectors.
141   * @param nominalDt Nominal discretization timestep in seconds.
142   */
143  public UnscentedKalmanFilter(
144      SigmaPoints<States> pts,
145      Nat<States> states,
146      Nat<Outputs> outputs,
147      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> f,
148      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>> h,
149      Matrix<States, N1> stateStdDevs,
150      Matrix<Outputs, N1> measurementStdDevs,
151      BiFunction<Matrix<States, ?>, Matrix<?, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> meanFuncX,
152      BiFunction<Matrix<Outputs, ?>, Matrix<?, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>> meanFuncY,
153      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> residualFuncX,
154      BiFunction<Matrix<Outputs, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>, Matrix<Outputs, N1>> residualFuncY,
155      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> addFuncX,
156      double nominalDt) {
157    this.m_states = states;
158    this.m_outputs = outputs;
159
160    m_f = f;
161    m_h = h;
162
163    m_meanFuncX = meanFuncX;
164    m_meanFuncY = meanFuncY;
165    m_residualFuncX = residualFuncX;
166    m_residualFuncY = residualFuncY;
167    m_addFuncX = addFuncX;
168
169    m_dt = nominalDt;
170
171    m_contQ = StateSpaceUtil.covarianceMatrix(states, stateStdDevs);
172    m_contR = StateSpaceUtil.covarianceMatrix(outputs, measurementStdDevs);
173
174    m_pts = pts;
175
176    reset();
177    MathSharedStore.getMathShared().reportUsage("UnscentedKalmanFilter", "");
178  }
179
180  static <C extends Num> Pair<Matrix<C, N1>, Matrix<C, C>> squareRootUnscentedTransform(
181      Nat<C> covdim,
182      int numSigmas,
183      Matrix<C, ?> sigmas,
184      Matrix<?, N1> Wm,
185      Matrix<?, N1> Wc,
186      BiFunction<Matrix<C, ?>, Matrix<?, N1>, Matrix<C, N1>> meanFunc,
187      BiFunction<Matrix<C, N1>, Matrix<C, N1>, Matrix<C, N1>> residualFunc,
188      Matrix<C, C> squareRootR) {
189    if (sigmas.getNumRows() != covdim.getNum() || sigmas.getNumCols() != numSigmas) {
190      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
191          "Sigmas must be covDim by numSigmas! Got "
192              + sigmas.getNumRows()
193              + " by "
194              + sigmas.getNumCols());
195    }
196
197    if (Wm.getNumRows() != numSigmas || Wm.getNumCols() != 1) {
198      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
199          "Wm must be numSigmas by 1! Got " + Wm.getNumRows() + " by " + Wm.getNumCols());
200    }
201
202    if (Wc.getNumRows() != numSigmas || Wc.getNumCols() != 1) {
203      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
204          "Wc must be numSigmas by 1! Got " + Wc.getNumRows() + " by " + Wc.getNumCols());
205    }
206
207    // New mean is usually just the sum of the sigmas * weights:
208    //
209    //      2n
210    //   x̂ = Σ Wᵢ⁽ᵐ⁾𝒳ᵢ
211    //      i=0
212    //
213    // equations (19) and (23) in the paper show this,
214    // but we allow a custom function, usually for angle wrapping
215    Matrix<C, N1> x = meanFunc.apply(sigmas, Wm);
216
217    // Form an intermediate matrix S⁻ as:
218    //
219    //   [√{W₁⁽ᶜ⁾}(𝒳_{1:2L} - x̂) √{Rᵛ}]
220    //
221    // the part of equations (20) and (24) within the "qr{}"
222    //
223    // Note that we allow a custom function instead of the difference to allow
224    // angle wrapping. Furthermore, we allow an arbitrary number of sigma points to
225    // support similar methods such as the Scaled Spherical Simplex Filter (S3F).
226    Matrix<C, ?> Sbar =
227        new Matrix<>(new SimpleMatrix(covdim.getNum(), numSigmas - 1 + covdim.getNum()));
228    for (int i = 0; i < numSigmas - 1; i++) {
229      Sbar.setColumn(
230          i,
231          residualFunc.apply(sigmas.extractColumnVector(1 + i), x).times(Math.sqrt(Wc.get(1, 0))));
232    }
233    Sbar.assignBlock(0, numSigmas - 1, squareRootR);
234
235    QRDecompositionHouseholder_DDRM qr = new QRDecompositionHouseholder_DDRM();
236    var qrStorage = Sbar.transpose().getStorage();
237
238    if (!qr.decompose(qrStorage.getDDRM())) {
239      throw new RuntimeException("QR decomposition failed! Input matrix:\n" + qrStorage);
240    }
241
242    // Compute the square-root covariance of the sigma points
243    //
244    // We transpose S⁻ first because we formed it by horizontally
245    // concatenating each part; it should be vertical so we can take
246    // the QR decomposition as defined in the "QR Decomposition" passage
247    // of section 3. "EFFICIENT SQUARE-ROOT IMPLEMENTATION"
248    //
249    // The resulting matrix R is the square-root covariance S, but it
250    // is upper triangular, so we need to transpose it.
251    //
252    // equations (20) and (24)
253    Matrix<C, C> newS = new Matrix<>(new SimpleMatrix(qr.getR(null, true)).transpose());
254
255    // Update or downdate the square-root covariance with (𝒳₀-x̂)
256    // depending on whether its weight (W₀⁽ᶜ⁾) is positive or negative.
257    //
258    // equations (21) and (25)
259    newS.rankUpdate(residualFunc.apply(sigmas.extractColumnVector(0), x), Wc.get(0, 0), true);
260
261    return new Pair<>(x, newS);
262  }

264  /**
265   * Returns the square-root error covariance matrix S.
266   *
267   * @return the square-root error covariance matrix S.
268   */
269  public Matrix<States, States> getS() {
270    return m_S;
271  }
272
273  /**
274   * Returns an element of the square-root error covariance matrix S.
275   *
276   * @param row Row of S.
277   * @param col Column of S.
278   * @return the value of the square-root error covariance matrix S at (i, j).
279   */
280  public double getS(int row, int col) {
281    return m_S.get(row, col);
282  }

284  /**
285   * Sets the entire square-root error covariance matrix S.
286   *
287   * @param newS The new value of S to use.
288   */
289  public void setS(Matrix<States, States> newS) {
290    m_S = newS;
291  }

293  /**
294   * Returns the reconstructed error covariance matrix P.
295   *
296   * @return the error covariance matrix P.
297   */
298  @Override
299  public Matrix<States, States> getP() {
300    return m_S.times(m_S.transpose());
301  }
302
303  /**
304   * Returns an element of the error covariance matrix P.
305   *
306   * @param row Row of P.
307   * @param col Column of P.
308   * @return the value of the error covariance matrix P at (i, j).
309   * @throws UnsupportedOperationException indexing into the reconstructed P matrix is not supported
310   */
311  @Override
312  public double getP(int row, int col) {
313    throw new UnsupportedOperationException(
314        "indexing into the reconstructed P matrix is not supported");
315  }
316
317  /**
318   * Sets the entire error covariance matrix P.
319   *
320   * @param newP The new value of P to use.
321   */
322  @Override
323  public void setP(Matrix<States, States> newP) {
324    m_S = newP.lltDecompose(true);
325  }

369  /** Resets the observer. */
370  @Override
371  public final void reset() {
372    m_xHat = new Matrix<>(m_states, Nat.N1());
373    m_S = new Matrix<>(m_states, m_states);
374    m_sigmasF = new Matrix<>(new SimpleMatrix(m_states.getNum(), m_pts.getNumSigmas()));
375  }
376
377  /**
378   * Project the model into the future with a new control input u.
379   *
380   * @param u New control input from controller.
381   * @param dt Timestep for prediction in seconds.
382   */
383  @Override
384  public void predict(Matrix<Inputs, N1> u, double dt) {
385    // Discretize Q before projecting mean and covariance forward
386    Matrix<States, States> contA =
387        NumericalJacobian.numericalJacobianX(m_states, m_states, m_f, m_xHat, u);
388    var discQ = Discretization.discretizeAQ(contA, m_contQ, dt).getSecond();
389    var squareRootDiscQ = discQ.lltDecompose(true);
390
391    // Generate sigma points around the state mean
392    //
393    // equation (17)
394    var sigmas = m_pts.squareRootSigmaPoints(m_xHat, m_S);
395
396    // Project each sigma point forward in time according to the
397    // dynamics f(x, u)
398    //
399    //   sigmas  = 𝒳ₖ₋₁
400    //   sigmasF = 𝒳ₖ,ₖ₋₁ or just 𝒳 for readability
401    //
402    // equation (18)
403    for (int i = 0; i < m_pts.getNumSigmas(); ++i) {
404      Matrix<States, N1> x = sigmas.extractColumnVector(i);
405
406      m_sigmasF.setColumn(i, NumericalIntegration.rk4(m_f, x, u, dt));
407    }
408
409    // Pass the predicted sigmas (𝒳) through the Unscented Transform
410    // to compute the prior state mean and covariance
411    //
412    // equations (18) (19) and (20)
413    var ret =
414        squareRootUnscentedTransform(
415            m_states,
416            m_pts.getNumSigmas(),
417            m_sigmasF,
418            m_pts.getWm(),
419            m_pts.getWc(),
420            m_meanFuncX,
421            m_residualFuncX,
422            squareRootDiscQ);
423
424    m_xHat = ret.getFirst();
425    m_S = ret.getSecond();
426    m_dt = dt;
427  }
428
429  /**
430   * Correct the state estimate x-hat using the measurements in y.
431   *
432   * @param u Same control input used in the predict step.
433   * @param y Measurement vector.
434   */
435  @Override
436  public void correct(Matrix<Inputs, N1> u, Matrix<Outputs, N1> y) {
437    correct(
438        m_outputs, u, y, m_h, m_contR, m_meanFuncY, m_residualFuncY, m_residualFuncX, m_addFuncX);
439  }
440
441  /**
442   * Correct the state estimate x-hat using the measurements in y.
443   *
444   * <p>This is useful for when the measurement noise covariances vary.
445   *
446   * @param u Same control input used in the predict step.
447   * @param y Measurement vector.
448   * @param R Continuous measurement noise covariance matrix.
449   */
450  public void correct(Matrix<Inputs, N1> u, Matrix<Outputs, N1> y, Matrix<Outputs, Outputs> R) {
451    correct(m_outputs, u, y, m_h, R, m_meanFuncY, m_residualFuncY, m_residualFuncX, m_addFuncX);
452  }
453
454  /**
455   * Correct the state estimate x-hat using the measurements in y.
456   *
457   * <p>This is useful for when the measurements available during a timestep's Correct() call vary.
458   * The h(x, u) passed to the constructor is used if one is not provided (the two-argument version
459   * of this function).
460   *
461   * @param <R> Number of measurements in y.
462   * @param rows Number of rows in y.
463   * @param u Same control input used in the predict step.
464   * @param y Measurement vector.
465   * @param h A vector-valued function of x and u that returns the measurement vector.
466   * @param R Continuous measurement noise covariance matrix.
467   */
468  public <R extends Num> void correct(
469      Nat<R> rows,
470      Matrix<Inputs, N1> u,
471      Matrix<R, N1> y,
472      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>> h,
473      Matrix<R, R> R) {
474    BiFunction<Matrix<R, ?>, Matrix<?, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>> meanFuncY =
475        (sigmas, Wm) -> sigmas.times(Matrix.changeBoundsUnchecked(Wm));
476    BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> residualFuncX =
477        Matrix::minus;
478    BiFunction<Matrix<R, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>> residualFuncY = Matrix::minus;
479    BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> addFuncX = Matrix::plus;
480    correct(rows, u, y, h, R, meanFuncY, residualFuncY, residualFuncX, addFuncX);
481  }
482
483  /**
484   * Correct the state estimate x-hat using the measurements in y.
485   *
486   * <p>This is useful for when the measurements available during a timestep's Correct() call vary.
487   * The h(x, u) passed to the constructor is used if one is not provided (the two-argument version
488   * of this function).
489   *
490   * @param <R> Number of measurements in y.
491   * @param rows Number of rows in y.
492   * @param u Same control input used in the predict step.
493   * @param y Measurement vector.
494   * @param h A vector-valued function of x and u that returns the measurement vector.
495   * @param R Continuous measurement noise covariance matrix.
496   * @param meanFuncY A function that computes the mean of NumSigmas measurement vectors using a
497   *     given set of weights.
498   * @param residualFuncY A function that computes the residual of two measurement vectors (i.e. it
499   *     subtracts them.)
500   * @param residualFuncX A function that computes the residual of two state vectors (i.e. it
501   *     subtracts them.)
502   * @param addFuncX A function that adds two state vectors.
503   */
504  public <R extends Num> void correct(
505      Nat<R> rows,
506      Matrix<Inputs, N1> u,
507      Matrix<R, N1> y,
508      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<Inputs, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>> h,
509      Matrix<R, R> R,
510      BiFunction<Matrix<R, ?>, Matrix<?, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>> meanFuncY,
511      BiFunction<Matrix<R, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>, Matrix<R, N1>> residualFuncY,
512      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> residualFuncX,
513      BiFunction<Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>, Matrix<States, N1>> addFuncX) {
514    final var discR = Discretization.discretizeR(R, m_dt);
515    final var squareRootDiscR = discR.lltDecompose(true);
516
517    // Generate new sigma points from the prior mean and covariance
518    // and transform them into measurement space using h(x, u)
519    //
520    //   sigmas  = 𝒳
521    //   sigmasH = 𝒴
522    //
523    // This differs from equation (22) which uses
524    // the prior sigma points, regenerating them allows
525    // multiple measurement updates per time update
526    Matrix<R, ?> sigmasH = new Matrix<>(new SimpleMatrix(rows.getNum(), m_pts.getNumSigmas()));
527    var sigmas = m_pts.squareRootSigmaPoints(m_xHat, m_S);
528    for (int i = 0; i < m_pts.getNumSigmas(); i++) {
529      Matrix<R, N1> hRet = h.apply(sigmas.extractColumnVector(i), u);
530      sigmasH.setColumn(i, hRet);
531    }
532
533    // Pass the predicted measurement sigmas through the Unscented Transform
534    // to compute the mean predicted measurement and square-root innovation
535    // covariance.
536    //
537    // equations (23) (24) and (25)
538    var transRet =
539        squareRootUnscentedTransform(
540            rows,
541            m_pts.getNumSigmas(),
542            sigmasH,
543            m_pts.getWm(),
544            m_pts.getWc(),
545            meanFuncY,
546            residualFuncY,
547            squareRootDiscR);
548    var yHat = transRet.getFirst();
549    var Sy = transRet.getSecond();
550
551    // Compute cross covariance of the predicted state and measurement sigma
552    // points given as:
553    //
554    //           2n
555    //   P_{xy} = Σ Wᵢ⁽ᶜ⁾[𝒳ᵢ - x̂][𝒴ᵢ - ŷ⁻]ᵀ
556    //           i=0
557    //
558    // equation (26)
559    Matrix<States, R> Pxy = new Matrix<>(m_states, rows);
560    for (int i = 0; i < m_pts.getNumSigmas(); i++) {
561      var dx = residualFuncX.apply(m_sigmasF.extractColumnVector(i), m_xHat);
562      var dy = residualFuncY.apply(sigmasH.extractColumnVector(i), yHat).transpose();
563
564      Pxy = Pxy.plus(dx.times(dy).times(m_pts.getWc(i)));
565    }
566
567    // Compute the Kalman gain. We use Eigen's QR decomposition to solve. This
568    // is equivalent to MATLAB's \ operator, so we need to rearrange to use
569    // that.
570    //
571    //   K = (P_{xy} / S_{y}ᵀ) / S_{y}
572    //   K = (S_{y} \ P_{xy})ᵀ / S_{y}
573    //   K = (S_{y}ᵀ \ (S_{y} \ P_{xy}ᵀ))ᵀ
574    //
575    // equation (27)
576    Matrix<States, R> K =
577        Sy.transpose()
578            .solveFullPivHouseholderQr(Sy.solveFullPivHouseholderQr(Pxy.transpose()))
579            .transpose();
580
581    // Compute the posterior state mean
582    //
583    // x̂ = x̂⁻ + K(y − ŷ⁻)
584    //
585    // second part of equation (27)
586    m_xHat = addFuncX.apply(m_xHat, K.times(residualFuncY.apply(y, yHat)));
587
588    // Compute the intermediate matrix U for downdating
589    // the square-root covariance
590    //
591    // equation (28)
592    Matrix<States, R> U = K.times(Sy);
593
594    // Downdate the posterior square-root state covariance
595    //
596    // equation (29)
597    for (int i = 0; i < rows.getNum(); i++) {
598      m_S.rankUpdate(U.extractColumnVector(i), -1, true);
599    }
600  }
601}
